newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks lower on Dow, gold, copper falls.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks lower on Dow, gold, copper falls.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 93.280 +0.005 Gold NY 318.25 Lon fix 317.30
*Shares lower on Dow fall and weaker gold and copper prices, trade quiet ahead of jobs data. Volume 37.38 million, value A$68.76 million, 543 stocks traded, 203 steady, 76 up, 263 down.

Australian shares opened weaker on Thursday after a 120 point drop on Wall Street and further falls in the gold and copper prices, but trade was quiet ahead of June employment data due out at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).

At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 23.2 points down at 2,672.9, while the September share price index futures contracts was 29 points lower at 2,692, narrowing the premium to the underlying index to 19.1 points.
Brokers said the market is likely to settle between 10 and 20 points lower, with the June jobs data unlikely to have much impact, unless the figures are outside the forecast range.
Unemployment rose to 8.8 percent in May and economists are expecting the jobless rate to be 8.7 percent in June.
"Wall Street is off 120 so I think there will be a few fireworks around," said one Melbourne-based broker. The Dow industrials failed to hit the 8,000 mark and ended at 7,842.
The gold price lost all of its gains from Tuesday's bounce, while the copper price neared four-and-a-half year lows.

"I don't think anybody really expected the gold price to do any serious bouncing and as far as the copper price is concerned, I think people have pulled back the expectations on the copper outlook," the broker said.
Gold miners Newcrest and Normandy topped the turnover lists on Thursday, with Newcrest losing ground but Normandy remaining unchanged.
Resource sectors fell harder than the industrials. Rio Tinto, BHP and WMC, all of which have copper operations, were the biggest fallers amongst the miners.
The largest fallers amongst the blue-chips was Coca-Cola Amatil and Brambles Industries Ltd.
Brokers said both stocks, which regularly have big price movements, had a strong run recently, but the falls were in light volume.
Banks were all lower after Wednesday's strong gains.

In the Australian bond market, yields were little changed from the previous day's low levels as the market awaited the jobs data. At 10.55 a.m. (0055 GMT), the 10-year T-bond was one percentage point down at 6.72 percent.
At the same time, the Australian dollar was trading at US$.7441/46, compared with Wednesday's close of $0.7435/40.
The local dollar was above the week's 18-month low of US$0.7413, but vulnerable after failing to sustain a short covering rally.
